stem.text: The electron micrograph shows onion root cells prepared using a freeze-fracture technique. The cells were quickly frozen and then physically broken apart. Freeze fracture breaks apart cells along weak areas, such as membranes and the surfaces of organelles.

stem.alt: Freeze-fracture electron micrograph of onion root cells, magnification ×20 000; a leader line labelled structure X points to small granular structures.

stem.text: Which statement best explains the appearance of the electron micrograph?

A.text: The cells were broken apart at the endoplasmic reticulum; structure X is a ribosome.

B.text: The cells were broken apart at the nuclear envelope; structure X is a nuclear pore.

C.text: The cells were broken apart at the nuclear envelope; structure X is a ribosome.

D.text: The cells were broken apart at the tonoplast; structure X is a plasmodesma.
